content: Kwantlen University College, commonly referred to as Kwantlen, is an undergraduate institution that grants degrees and operates across four campuses in the South Fraser region of British Columbia’s Lower Mainland. History Beginnings Kwantlen College was established in 1981 following its separation from Douglas College. In 1995, the British Columbia provincial government passed legislation to rename the institution Kwantlen University College, granting it the authority to confer academic degrees. The name Kwantlen translates to Tireless Runner and originates from the Kwantlen First Nation, a tribe historically rooted in the areas served by the institution. The name was selected by Stan McKinnon, who won a contest to name the new school. Expansion and Growth Transition to University In 2005, Kwantlen began advocating for its transition to a special-purpose university by engaging municipal and provincial officials, as well as influential community leaders. This transition required approval from the British Columbia government to remove college from its official name. Many students supported this change, as it would enhance their academic credentials and facilitate their entry into graduate programs and other professional pursuits. Kwantlen argued that becoming a university would: Strengthen its ability to contribute to British Columbia’s goal of becoming the most educated and literate jurisdiction in North America. Provide significant benefits to the rapidly growing region of British Columbia, supporting long-term growth and prosperity. In 2007, Murray Coell, the Minister of Advanced Education, and Geoff Plant, a special advisor, released the Campus 2020 report, which recommended that Kwantlen University College transition into Kwantlen University, a regional university. AUCC Membership In addition to its efforts to become a university, Kwantlen sought membership in the Association of Universities and Colleges of Canada (AUCC). Although AUCC is not an official government accreditation body, its membership standards indirectly facilitate the transfer of students from undergraduate to graduate programs across Canada and internationally. Academics Profile In 2006, Kwantlen had an enrollment exceeding 16,000 students. The institution serves a region with a population of over 775,000, including Richmond, Delta, Surrey, White Rock, and Langley. Despite this, the provincial government funds only 8,500 full-time equivalent student spaces (FTEs), which is the lowest per capita FTE funding in the province, at less than 60% of the provincial average. Faculty and Employees Kwantlen employs over 1,400 faculty and staff members. While some faculty engage in research, their primary focus is undergraduate education. In 2007, Kwantlen University College was recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers by Maclean’s magazine, making it the only community college in Canada to receive this distinction. Undergraduate Programs Kwantlen offers a variety of academic credentials, including bachelor’s degrees, associate degrees, diplomas, certificates, and citations. These programs span disciplines such as fine arts, humanities, sciences, social sciences, applied communication, business, nursing, and various technical and trade fields. Cooperative Education Several diploma and degree programs at Kwantlen include cooperative education components. These programs integrate dedicated work-placement semesters aligned with students’ fields of study, in addition to regular coursework. Program Transferability Kwantlen provides numerous transferable courses to other educational institutions, often enabling direct entry into secondor third-year studies at other post-secondary institutions. To support this, Kwantlen participates in the BC Transfer Guide website, an online resource for planning and understanding course transfers within British Columbia’s post-secondary education system. New Program Development Kwantlen is actively developing additional major and minor programs in anthropology, business, fine arts, and geography. Other Programs CELTA at Kwantlen The Cambridge Certificate in English Language Teaching to Adults (CELTA) is the most widely recognized certification for English language teacher training worldwide. This practical course is designed for individuals with little or no prior training, equipping them with the knowledge, awareness, and skills necessary to begin a career in English language teaching. In 2004, over 7,000 candidates completed the certification at more than 250 centers globally. Key features of the CELTA course include: Global recognition in the field of English language teaching. Trainers who have undergone rigorous trainer-training programs. Inspection of every course by an assessor from the University of Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate. Availability of both full-time and part-time courses. A practical focus with concurrent teaching practicums observed by course trainers. Small class sizes with a low trainee-to-trainer ratio (6:1). The course emphasizes teaching English to adult learners at beginner to upper-intermediate levels and aims to: Teach the principles of effective teaching. Provide practical skills for teaching English to adult learners. Offer hands-on teaching practice. Build confidence in new teachers. The course is structured into five main units: 1. Learners and teachers, and the teaching and learning context. 2. Language analysis and awareness. 3. Language skills: reading, listening, speaking, and writing. 4. Planning and resources for different contexts. 5. Developing teaching skills and professionalism. Student Life The Kwantlen Student Association (KSA) is an elected student body that contributes to community life and allocates student funds to social, cultural, and entertainment programs. Through the KSA, students and other members of the Kwantlen community can access special discounts, including bus and train passes, discounted movie tickets, and seasonal offers. In 2005, Kwantlen launched an interactive component of its official website called The Digital Cafe, featuring promotional videos, music by Kwantlen students, and photographs showcasing campus life and academic programs. Campus Campus Locations Kwantlen operates the following campuses: Cloverdale Campus: 5500 180th Street, Surrey, BC. Surrey Campus: 12666 72nd Avenue, Surrey, BC. Richmond Campus: 8771 Lansdowne Road, Richmond, BC. Langley Campus: 20901 Langley Bypass, Langley, BC. Newton Campus: 13479 77th Avenue, Surrey, BC. Campus Expansion Projects Kwantlen is engaged in two major building expansion projects. The first involves constructing a new wing on the main Surrey campus, increasing its size by 11,000 m², or 42% of its current area. The second project is the development of a new campus in Cloverdale, a 17,200 m² facility designed to replace the aging Newton campus. The new Cloverdale campus can accommodate more than twice the number of students as the Newton campus. The first phase of this campus opened in January 2007.
